title: A Archive for the Signal
premise: Tamsin Villalobos has spent nine years alone in the Svalbard-Adjunct seed vault, tending crops and a beacon whose origin no one will explain. When a derelict ship that never flew appears in orbit carrying a manifest with her mother's name, Tamsin learns the beacon is an inheritance: her family were the designated neutral couriers of a peace protocol both warring factions have spent decades trying to erase. Hunted by the Concord's inquisitor Kestrel and the Meridian fleet, she must carry the message to a relay only she can activate — at the cost of revealing that her dead lover, a Concord officer, encoded half of it. In the end Tamsin broadcasts the truth of both sides' shared origins, ending the war but dissolving the archives' neutrality forever, and chooses to stay on Earth as its first witness rather than its last caretaker.
about_author: J. M. Dravenmoor is the pen name of a former archivist who spent a decade cataloguing obsolete agricultural records before turning to fiction. They write quiet, character-driven science fiction about the people history forgets to record.

chapters.title: The Beacon Nobody Ordered
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Establishes her solitary routine in the seed vault: tending potatoes, logging the beacon's nightly pulse, talking to the plants. A supply drone arrives months late with a corrupted manifest. Emotional beat: loneliness worn smooth into ritual, and the first hairline crack in it.

chapters.title: A Ship That Never Flew
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The drone's manifest lists the Meridian courier vessel Halcyon — decommissioned before launch, crew of one: E. Villalobos. Tamsin cross-checks records and finds her own name appended as 'heir.' She pings the orbital registry; the ship is real, and inbound. Beat: dread blooming inside routine.

chapters.title: Docking Clearance Denied
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV, aboard a Concord interceptor shadowing the Halcyon. The inquisitor reads the same manifest anomaly and orders silent pursuit, forbidden from firing on a heritage vessel. Beat: cold professional curiosity curdling into obsession.

chapters.title: Mother's Voice
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The Halcyon docks itself; inside is a sealed archive core and a recorded message from her mother, presumed dead twenty years: 'If you're hearing this, the war found you anyway.' The core requires two keys — one genetic, one given. Beat: grief reopened as inheritance.

chapters.title: The First Key
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Her blood unlocks half the core: star charts showing Earth seeded by both warring factions from a common origin. The message fragment names a relay station in the Kuiper belt. Beat: vertigo — her whole identity reframed as custodianship of a secret.

chapters.title: Interception
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. The Concord boards the vault under pretense of inspection. Tamsin hides the core in the seed stacks among ten thousand identical canisters. Kestrel interviews her and leaves unconvinced. Beat: cat-and-mouse tension; Tamsin discovers she can lie well.

chapters.title: What I Buried
chapters.summary: Flashback chapter, Tamsin's POV. Nine years ago: her lover Ilan, a Concord signals officer, discovered the beacon's frequency matched Meridian prayer-chants and chose exile with her rather than report it. His disappearance three years ago was ruled desertion. Beat: love remembered as complicity.

chapters.title: The Second Key
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The core demands a second key: 'given, not inherited.' She realizes it's a cipher phrase — and recognizes Ilan's cadence in the error messages. He helped build this. He may still be alive. Beat: hope arriving like an accusation.

chapters.title: Kestrel's Ledger
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Interrogating vault records, Kestrel finds Ilan's name in the beacon's maintenance logs — the deserter was here. Personal stakes ignite: Kestrel trained him. Beat: duty beginning to chafe against doubt.

chapters.title: Burn the Vault
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Concord forces return to seize the archive. Tamsin triggers the vault's fire-suppression blackout, plunging everything into darkness, and escapes via the old seed-exchange tunnel with the core. Beat: the caretaker burning what she swore to keep.

chapters.title: The Long Dark
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV, alone in the subglacial tunnels. Frostbite, rationing, hallucinations of Ilan's voice guiding her toward a buried emergency skiff. Beat: endurance stripped to essentials; she stops being a caretaker and becomes a courier.

chapters.title: Meridian Hospitality
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The skiff is scooped up by a Meridian patrol. Their captain, Oyelaran, treats her courteously — and reveals they've been waiting for a Villalobos for thirty years. They want the message delivered their way. Beat: rescue that feels like capture.

chapters.title: Two Keys, Two Masters
chapters.summary: Oyelaran's POV. The captain explains the message proves both factions descend from the same colony fleet — peace or annihilation. But Meridian plans to edit the broadcast to blame Concord. Tamsin realizes delivering the message isn't enough; it must be whole. Beat: allies revealed as another kind of cage.

chapters.title: Signal Ghost
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Decoding the second key with Meridian cryptographers, she reconstructs Ilan's cipher phrase: 'the garden remembers the gardener.' The core completes — and displays his final log entry, dated after his disappearance. He's alive, held somewhere in the Concord core worlds. Beat: the message and the man entwined.

chapters.title: Bargaining Chip
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Concord command, tipped off, captures the Meridian convoy. Kestrel comes face to face with Tamsin and offers a trade: the core for Ilan's release. Tamsin sees the offer is real — and that Concord will still edit the message. Beat: love against duty made literal.

chapters.title: The Relay
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. Both fleets converge on the Kuiper relay station, the only transmitter powerful enough. Tamsin, escorted by Kestrel under truce, begins activation while captains argue over authorship of the truth. Beat: rising dread; countdown to mutual fleet engagement.

chapters.title: Ilan
chapters.summary: Alternating Tamsin/Ilan POV. Ilan, imprisoned aboard a Concord flagship, broadcasts the cipher phrase on open channels — his half of the key, spoken aloud so neither side can claim sole possession. Tamsin hears his voice through static. Beat: love completing what inheritance began.

chapters.title: Broadcast
chapters.summary: Climax, multiple POVs. Tamsin transmits the unedited message fleet-wide: shared origin, shared guilt, shared seeds. Weapons hold. Kestrel, ordered to jam the signal, instead relays it to the Concord home fleet. Beat: catharsis — truth as the only neutral party.

chapters.title: Aftermath of Light
chapters.summary: Kestrel's POV. Ceasefire negotiations begin in the relay's shadow. Kestrel faces censure for disobedience and accepts it without regret, finally meeting Ilan. Beat: duty redefined as conscience.

chapters.title: Return to the Vault
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. She comes home to a damaged, darkened vault and begins repairs — not alone now; Oyelaran sends aid convoys, and Ilan is coming on the first one. Beat: exhaustion transformed into cautious joy.

chapters.title: New Manifest
chapters.summary: Tamsin's POV. The vault is redesignated an open archive: seeds, records, and the full war message, available to all. Tamsin writes the new manifest herself and adds two names beside her mother's. Beat: inheritance fulfilled by giving it away.

chapters.title: First Witness
chapters.summary: Final chapter, Tamsin's POV, years later. She walks the restored fields with Ilan, teaching new arrivals the old routines. The beacon still pulses nightly — not a warning now, but a greeting. Beat: peace as ongoing work, and solitude finally chosen rather than imposed.
